section_summary: This section records U.S. responses to proposed visits by the Japanese scouting ship Hakuho Maru and training ship Hakuyo Maru to Alaskan ports in 1934 and 1935. It also contains reports on Japanese fishing vessels in the Bering Sea and a dispute between the State and Navy Departments over reciprocal access to ports in the Japanese Mandated Islands. In 1935, the Hakuyo Maru abandoned planned calls at Dutch Harbor and St. Paul Island after the Navy proposed placing an officer aboard and accompanying the ship in U.S. territorial waters.

subfiles.title: Closing page of letter concerning Hakuho Maru visits
subfiles.from: William Phillips, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State requests objections, if any, to Hakuho Maru visits and asks that customary courtesies be arranged.
subfiles.summary: Closing request for a departmental response and customary courtesies.

subfiles.title: State Department letter to the Secretary of the Navy on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.from: William Phillips, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State seeks Navy's view on proposed Hakuho Maru calls at Attu and Atka during a fur-seal survey.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese scouting ship plans to observe fur-seal migration near the western Aleutians. State asks whether Navy objects to its proposed calls and requests customary courtesies.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Japanese Ambassador on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: State acknowledges the proposed Hakuho Maru itinerary and says it is consulting other departments.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges the planned Attu and Atka calls and promises a further answer after consulting federal departments.

subfiles.title: Request to Department of Labor concerning Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: State requests customary courtesies for Hakuho Maru's proposed Aleutian calls.
subfiles.summary: Requests Labor's cooperation with the Hakuho Maru visits.

subfiles.title: Request to Treasury concerning Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: State requests customary courtesies for Hakuho Maru's proposed Aleutian calls.
subfiles.summary: Requests Treasury's cooperation with the Hakuho Maru visits.

subfiles.title: Request to Interior concerning Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: State requests customary courtesies for Hakuho Maru's proposed Aleutian calls.
subfiles.summary: Requests Interior's cooperation with the Hakuho Maru visits.

subfiles.title: Request to Agriculture concerning Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: State requests customary courtesies for Hakuho Maru's proposed Aleutian calls.
subfiles.summary: Requests Agriculture's cooperation with the Hakuho Maru visits.

subfiles.title: Approval of Hakuho Maru visits
subfiles.about: State informs Japan that Hakuho Maru's proposed Attu and Atka visits are agreeable.
subfiles.summary: Approves the visits and says customary courtesies have been arranged.

subfiles.title: Commerce response on proposed Hakuyo Maru cruise
subfiles.about: Commerce reports prior Hakuyo Maru calls and no objection to renewed visits if formally requested.
subfiles.summary: Commerce notes earlier Dutch Harbor and St. Paul visits and offers customary courtesies.

subfiles.title: Labor acknowledgment of Hakuyo Maru cruise
subfiles.from: Deputy Commissioner, Immigration and Naturalization Service
subfiles.about: Labor says immigration authorities have been informed of Hakuyo Maru's planned cruise.
subfiles.summary: Immigration authorities have been advised of the cruise.

subfiles.title: Navy acknowledgment of Hakuyo Maru visits
subfiles.from: Claude A. Swanson, Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Navy agrees to notify commanders about Hakuyo Maru's Bristol Bay and St. Paul visits.
subfiles.summary: Navy will arrange the usual courtesies and facilities.

subfiles.title: Commerce arrangements for Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.about: Commerce will direct fisheries staff to assist Hakuyo Maru at St. Paul and other Alaskan calls.
subfiles.summary: Fisheries personnel will extend customary courtesies where the vessel calls.

subfiles.title: Commerce approval of Hakuho Maru calls
subfiles.about: Commerce raises no objection to Hakuho Maru's visits to Chichagof Harbor and Nazan Bay.
subfiles.summary: Commerce approves the calls and promises courtesies if fisheries vessels are present.

subfiles.title: Interior response on Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.from: First Assistant Secretary of the Interior
subfiles.about: Interior has no objection to Hakuyo Maru's Alaskan calls and has notified Alaska's governor.
subfiles.summary: Interior reports no objection and notification of the governor.

subfiles.title: Japanese thanks for Hakuyo Maru arrangements
subfiles.about: The Ambassador thanks State for arranging courtesies for Hakuyo Maru at Dutch Harbor and St. Paul.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges and appreciates the arrangements.

subfiles.title: Navy letter on Aleutian access and Japanese Mandated Islands
subfiles.about: Navy questions allowing Japanese public vessels into the Aleutians without reciprocal U.S. naval access to Japanese mandated ports.
subfiles.summary: Navy does not formally object to the Hakuho Maru calls but considers unrestricted Japanese cruising in the Aleutians strategically undesirable. It reviews unsuccessful efforts to arrange U.S. naval visits to Wotje and other mandated islands and asks whether State will formally notify Japan of proposed visits.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conference with Navy officers
subfiles.about: A State officer records discussion of a draft reply on port-access rights with senior Navy officers.
subfiles.summary: At a July 3 conference, Navy officers read State's draft response. Admiral Standley thought it resolved the legal question and retained copies for further consideration.

subfiles.title: Instruction to retain draft letter in file
subfiles.about: A handwritten instruction says the attached Navy letter should be filed rather than sent.
subfiles.summary: Retain the draft in the file; do not send it.

subfiles.title: Note on legal basis for mandated-island port access
subfiles.about: A drafter notes earlier legal memoranda and discussion of U.S. naval access to Japanese mandated ports.
subfiles.summary: Earlier legal analysis should be addressed in writing to Navy.

subfiles.title: Draft State reply to Navy on mandated-island ports
subfiles.about: State argues that treaties provide insufficient legal grounds for unrestricted U.S. naval entry into closed mandated-island ports.
subfiles.summary: The draft examines the 1922 Treaty of Yap, Japan's mandate authority, and the 1911 commerce treaty. It concludes that Japan could restrict foreign vessels to open ports, while evidence of access granted to other foreign vessels might support a request for equivalent treatment. The pages appear out of textual order in the scan.

subfiles.title: Revised draft State reply to Navy
subfiles.about: A revised draft explains State's legal position on U.S. naval access to Japanese mandated ports.
subfiles.summary: State reasons that Japanese laws and existing U.S.–Japan treaties limit vessel access to designated open ports in the mandated islands. It finds inadequate legal grounds to contest exclusion from closed ports, though comparable privileges granted to another nation could justify a diplomatic approach. The draft also recalls a 1929 Navy–State discussion.

subfiles.title: Treasury arrangements for Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.about: Treasury authorizes the Juneau customs collector to assist Hakuyo Maru during its Alaskan visits.
subfiles.summary: The customs collector will extend customary courtesies.

subfiles.title: Japanese thanks for Hakuho Maru approval
subfiles.about: The Ambassador acknowledges U.S. approval of Hakuho Maru's Attu and Atka calls.
subfiles.summary: Thanks State and the authorities for approving and assisting the visits.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch transmitting Japanese fishing-vessel information
subfiles.about: The Tokyo Embassy forwards a Japanese Foreign Ministry letter on floating canneries bound for the Bering Sea.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the enclosed vessel report.

subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Ministry letter listing Bering Sea vessels
subfiles.about: Japan lists crab-canning ships, boats, and trawlers that departed Hakodate for the Bering Sea.
subfiles.summary: Nishi lists the Taihoku Maru, Nagato Maru, Kasado Maru, and their accessory craft. He says the vessels operate on the high seas and are not expected to enter American waters.

subfiles.title: Treasury arrangements for Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Treasury directs the Juneau customs collector to extend courtesies to Hakuho Maru.
subfiles.summary: The customs collector will assist the scouting ship.

subfiles.title: Labor arrangements for Hakuho Maru
subfiles.from: Deputy Commissioner, Immigration and Naturalization Service
subfiles.about: Labor instructs its Seattle district director to extend courtesies to Hakuho Maru.
subfiles.summary: Immigration authorities have received instructions.

subfiles.title: Telegram asking about Hakuyo Maru's Philippine calls
subfiles.about: A consul asks whether Hakuyo Maru needs diplomatic permission before visiting Davao and Manila.
subfiles.summary: Requests guidance on visa and health-document formalities.

subfiles.title: Handwritten comment on telegram reply
subfiles.about: A handwritten note suggests substituting another draft reply.
subfiles.summary: Suggests a substitute draft.

subfiles.title: Instructions to consul on Hakuyo Maru's Philippine calls
subfiles.about: State authorizes crew-list visas and a bill of health while avoiding a ruling on diplomatic permission.
subfiles.summary: Issue the documents without raising whether diplomatic permission is required.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch transmitting Fisheries Institute thanks
subfiles.about: Grew forwards the Tokyo Fisheries Institute's thanks for treatment of Hakuyo Maru in the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the Institute president's letter.

subfiles.title: Fisheries Institute letter of thanks
subfiles.about: The Institute president thanks U.S. authorities for assisting Hakuyo Maru at Davao and Manila.
subfiles.summary: Thanks American authorities and reports the ship's safe return to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Japanese request for 1935 Hakuyo Maru visits
subfiles.about: Japan requests permission and customary courtesies for Hakuyo Maru's planned Alaskan calls.
subfiles.summary: Captain Jinzo Nakagawa plans a training cruise with crew and students, including Bristol Bay, Dutch Harbor, and St. Paul Island. The Ambassador asks whether the visits and landings are agreeable.

subfiles.title: State acknowledgment of 1935 Hakuyo Maru request
subfiles.about: State acknowledges the requested Hakuyo Maru visits and consults federal departments.
subfiles.summary: State will answer after receiving departmental replies.

subfiles.title: Request to Agriculture on 1935 Hakuyo Maru visits
subfiles.about: State asks Agriculture to extend customary courtesies to Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Requests cooperation with the planned visits.

subfiles.title: Request to Commerce on 1935 Hakuyo Maru visits
subfiles.about: State asks Commerce to extend customary courtesies to Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Requests cooperation with the planned visits.

subfiles.title: Request to Interior on 1935 Hakuyo Maru visits
subfiles.about: State asks Interior to extend customary courtesies to Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Requests cooperation with the planned visits.

subfiles.title: Request to Labor on 1935 Hakuyo Maru visits
subfiles.about: State asks Labor to extend customary courtesies to Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Requests cooperation with the planned visits.

subfiles.title: Request to Treasury on 1935 Hakuyo Maru visits
subfiles.about: State asks Treasury to extend customary courtesies to Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Requests cooperation with the planned visits.

subfiles.title: Request to Navy on 1935 Hakuyo Maru visits
subfiles.about: State asks whether Navy objects to Hakuyo Maru's visits and requests customary courtesies.
subfiles.summary: Uses Navy's preferred wording concerning objections to the visits.

subfiles.title: Alternative form of request to Navy
subfiles.about: A parallel draft requests Navy's cooperation with the 1935 Hakuyo Maru calls.
subfiles.summary: Records an alternative wording of the Navy request.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on wording of Navy request
subfiles.about: Commander Lewis suggests adding 'to the visit' to prevent misunderstanding.
subfiles.summary: Records Navy's requested wording change.

subfiles.title: Protocol memorandum on Navy's preferred wording
subfiles.about: Protocol records Navy's objection to the standard wording of requests about foreign-vessel visits.
subfiles.summary: Navy wants objections framed specifically as objections to the visit.

subfiles.title: Protocol reply to Dooman
subfiles.about: Protocol agrees to alter wording despite an earlier Navy approval of its standard form.
subfiles.summary: Accepts Navy's requested change.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on fishing vessels near the Aleutians
subfiles.about: A State officer records Captain Alger's account of American cod vessels and Japanese ships in Alaskan waters.
subfiles.summary: Alger describes American cod schooners at Bristol Bay and Japanese cannery vessels nearby. He also discusses the Hakuho Maru's seal-observation mission and the Hakuyo Maru's earlier authorized calls.

subfiles.title: Commerce response on 1935 Hakuyo Maru calls
subfiles.about: Commerce will arrange fisheries staff courtesies for Hakuyo Maru's proposed Alaskan visits.
subfiles.summary: Commerce promises customary assistance at St. Paul and other relevant calls.

subfiles.title: Treasury response on 1935 Hakuyo Maru calls
subfiles.about: Treasury authorizes its Juneau customs collector to assist Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Customs will extend customary courtesies.

subfiles.title: Labor response on 1935 Hakuyo Maru calls
subfiles.from: Deputy Commissioner, Immigration and Naturalization Service
subfiles.about: Labor instructs its Seattle district director to assist Hakuyo Maru's personnel.
subfiles.summary: The district director will extend courtesies consistent with law.

subfiles.title: Navy reply on 1935 Hakuyo Maru visits
subfiles.from: Claude A. Swanson, Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Navy proposes monitoring Hakuyo Maru during its Alaskan visits because U.S. naval operations are planned nearby.
subfiles.summary: Navy raises security concerns but does not object outright. It proposes an American officer aboard, a U.S. vessel alongside, and exact itinerary details.

subfiles.title: Naval Operations transmittal of tentative draft
subfiles.about: Admiral Standley sends a tentative Navy reply for State's comment.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the draft at Standley's direction.

subfiles.title: Tentative Navy reply on Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.about: Navy outlines security conditions for Hakuyo Maru's proposed visits and raises reciprocal access to mandated islands.
subfiles.summary: The draft links Japanese visits to U.S. surveys in the Aleutians and suspected intelligence gathering. It proposes an American naval officer aboard and an escort vessel during territorial-water visits, asks for precise dates and ports, and mentions a future U.S. naval visit to Japanese mandated islands.

subfiles.title: Draft note to Japanese Ambassador on inconvenient visit dates
subfiles.about: State advises that U.S. naval activity complicates Hakuyo Maru's calls and proposes an officer aboard and an accompanying vessel.
subfiles.summary: The draft says the planned dates are inconvenient because American naval vessels may operate nearby. If Japan proceeds, State asks for exact dates and ports to arrange an officer aboard and a U.S. ship alongside.

subfiles.title: Handwritten revisions to Ambassador note
subfiles.from: Secretary and Under Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Fragmentary handwritten edits address the wording of the proposed note about Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Manuscript revisions to the diplomatic note.

subfiles.title: Revised opening of note to Japanese Ambassador
subfiles.about: A revised draft states that Hakuyo Maru's proposed visits would be inconvenient during U.S. naval activity.
subfiles.summary: Revised opening of the note on visit timing.

subfiles.title: Instruction concerning memorandum for Standley
subfiles.about: A note suggests delivering the attached memorandum to Admiral Standley through Commander Train.
subfiles.summary: Suggests delivery of the memorandum.

subfiles.title: State memorandum for Admiral Standley
subfiles.about: State comments on Navy's proposed Hakuyo Maru restrictions and its separate mandated-islands request.
subfiles.summary: State accepts Navy's statement that the visits are inconvenient and its plan to put an officer aboard the ship. It suggests handling the proposed U.S. naval visit to Japanese mandated islands in a separate letter, with named ports, and considers an approach to Japan inopportune at that time.

subfiles.title: Japanese cancellation of Hakuyo Maru port visits
subfiles.about: Japan cancels Hakuyo Maru's Dutch Harbor and St. Paul calls because the proposed U.S. arrangements are inconvenient.
subfiles.summary: The ship will practice fishing in open waters of Bristol Bay, then proceed to Russian waters.

subfiles.title: State notice to Navy of canceled Hakuyo Maru calls
subfiles.about: State informs Navy that Hakuyo Maru will not call at Dutch Harbor or St. Paul Island.
subfiles.summary: The ship will leave Bristol Bay's open-sea fishing grounds for Russian waters.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese crab-fishing vessels
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports the departure of Japanese vessels and accessory craft for Bering Sea crab fishing.
subfiles.summary: Ryokai Maru and Taihoku Maru departed Hakodate; fuller details will follow by mail.

subfiles.title: Protocol memorandum on fishing-vessel telegram
subfiles.from: Division of International Conferences and Protocol
subfiles.about: Protocol relates the new fishing-vessel report to earlier discussion of a Bering Sea salmon treaty.
subfiles.summary: Suggests Far Eastern Affairs consider the report.

subfiles.title: State notice to Navy of Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.about: State passes Navy the Embassy's report on Japanese crab-fishing vessels departing Hakodate for the Bering Sea.
subfiles.summary: Reports the Ryokai Maru, Taihoku Maru, and their accessory craft.
